title: Recovery 2.4-2.7 - one jumper on J13's SOP2 position
caption: For the boot loader: one jumper on the row printed 2 (SOP2), rows 1 and 0 open. Off again for a normal boot. Never 1 and 0 together.

callouts.label: row 2, SOP2: jumper ON for the boot loader
callouts.note: The row printed '2', the top row of the 2x3 header. One jumper across its two pins pulls SOP2 high: the CC3220's UART boot loader (likely, from the silkscreen; TI's guide SWRU463 not checked: unverified). Off again for a normal boot.

callouts.label: row 1, SOP1: open
callouts.note: The row printed '1', the middle row. No jumper. Rows 1 and 0 together select the return-to-factory-image mode, which writes the flash: never fit them at the same time (SWRU463 not checked: unverified).

callouts.label: row 0, SOP0: open
callouts.note: The row printed '0', the bottom row. No jumper.

callouts.label: Silkscreen 'J13', 'SOP' and rows '2 1 0'
callouts.note: 'SOP' and 'J13' above the header, the row numbers 2, 1, 0 down its left side (printed sideways). Where the jumpers sit now: the header is not empty in the photo (dark cap shapes over it), but which row a jumper bridges cannot be read; check on the board before the first boot.
